item.text: {"representations":[{"case_ref":"sample_3ebc9dd41fdddf5b","text":"Across March 30–April 12, sleep fell abruptly from the 28-day baseline mean of 464.5 to 346.2 minutes (−118.3; −25.5%). All 14 nights were shorter than the baseline range: 335–355 versus 455–475 minutes, with no return despite a small upward trend. Sleep onset shifted from about 22:55 to 00:54; waking remained 07:00. Weekends averaged 351 minutes versus 344.3 on weekdays, both substantially below baseline. Other daily means stayed close: steps 8,037 versus 7,983, active minutes 55.1 versus 55.6, low movement 451.6 versus 449.9, and RMSSD 44.9 versus 44.8 ms; resting heart rate was slightly lower, 55.4 versus 56.1 bpm. Activity remained at 21:00 for 50–60 minutes; daytime low movement comprised ten bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Activity duration and next-wake-date sleep showed little window association (r=−0.08, 13 pairs), versus −0.36 at baseline. No values were missing."},{"case_ref":"sample_e1879e777a2ec87c","text":"Throughout March 30–April 12, active minutes dropped from the 28-day baseline mean of 54.4 to 9.4 daily (−45; −82.8%), while low movement increased from 449.6 to 602 minutes (+152.4; +33.9%). These changes persisted on every day, including weekends, without recovery. The 21:00 activity bout shortened from 50–60 to 8–12 minutes. Low movement changed from ten 43–47-minute bouts to ten 59–61-minute bouts separated by five-minute gaps, extending from 10:00 to approximately 20:37–20:53 rather than around 18:00. Steps nevertheless remained stable at 8,029 versus 8,015 daily, with little association with active minutes (r=0.13). Sleep remained 470.6 versus 469.8 minutes, beginning around 22:49 and ending at 07:00, with virtually identical weekday/weekend means. Resting heart rate (55.9 versus 55.8 bpm) and RMSSD (44.9 versus 45.1 ms) also stayed near baseline. Activity and following sleep had a weak negative association (r=−0.29, 13 pairs). No values were missing."},{"case_ref":"sample_4bd546c39d8dc9d3","text":"A four-day change on April 3–6 interrupted otherwise baseline-like measurements: resting heart rate rose to 65–67 bpm versus the 28-day baseline mean of 56.0 (range 55–57), while RMSSD fell to 23–26 ms versus 45.0 (43–47). Both returned to baseline ranges on April 7 and remained there through April 12. Consequently, window means of 58.7 bpm and 38.9 ms obscure the local recovery. Their strong inverse window association (r=−0.97) reflects this simultaneous episode; the higher weekend heart rate and lower weekend RMSSD were concentrated in April 4–5, rather than repeated across both weekends. Sleep and movement showed no comparable episode: window versus baseline means were 470.4 versus 469.8 sleep minutes, 7,996 versus 8,043 steps, 55.3 versus 54.9 active minutes, and 446.6 versus 450.7 low-movement minutes. Sleep remained around 22:50–07:00; activity began at 21:00, and daytime low movement retained interrupted bouts. Activity and following sleep were weakly related (r=0.10, 13 pairs). No values were missing."},{"case_ref":"sample_7c5ba32ffe7d3c25","text":"Every day of March 30–April 12 had 480 low-movement minutes, up from the 28-day baseline mean of 449.3 (+30.8; +6.8%), with a larger change in continuity. Ten baseline bouts of 43–47 minutes separated by five-minute gaps became three continuous bouts: 10:00–12:30, 12:45–15:25, and 15:40–18:30 (150, 160, and 170 minutes), separated by 15-minute gaps. This structure persisted across both weekdays and weekends, without return. Other means remained close to baseline: steps 8,038 versus 8,026, active minutes 55.3 versus 55.3, sleep 471.1 versus 469.8 minutes, resting heart rate 55.9 versus 55.9 bpm, and RMSSD 45.6 versus 45.4 ms. Steps had a downward fitted window trend (−29/day) but remained within the baseline range. Activity continued at 21:00; sleep onset stayed around 22:49 with 07:00 waking and little weekday/weekend difference. Activity and following sleep had only a weak association (r=0.25, 13 pairs); other paired relationships were also weak. No values were missing."}]}
